source.title: The Impact of Geometric Complexity on Neural Collapse in Transfer Learning
source.authors: Michael Munn; Benoit Dherin; Javier Gonzalvo

record.tranche_reason: Tests whether a measured network property tracks held-out performance, using geometric complexity and neural collapse rather than the sharpness measure in V7.
record.gate_note: The paper reports that lower geometric complexity correlates with higher test accuracy. Its exact plotted values are figure-only. It does not test random-label memorization, width, architecture comparisons, optimizer comparisons, large-batch generalization gaps, dropout, magnitude-aware sharpness, or memorized-example removal.
record.test_reason: The study measures embedding geometric complexity, neural collapse and transfer accuracy, rather than any listed version's specified effect. These are not magnitude-aware weight sharpness (V7). Its batch-size sweep uses 100,000 training steps, so epochs vary with batch size and it does not test V5's fixed-epoch comparison.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate but abbreviated: the authors connect embedding geometric complexity with neural collapse through theory and experiments, and report that lower source complexity accompanies better few-shot transfer. Their theoretical transfer interpretation requires source–target compatibility assumptions; extension to language modeling remains unresolved.
record.recipe_differences: Measures geometric complexity and neural collapse, rather than the interventions or measures in the listed claim versions.
record.method_sensitivity: The plotted relationship is examined across learning-rate, batch-size, and L2-regularization sweeps.

fits_no_version.finding: For VGG-13 on CIFAR-10, lower embedding geometric complexity correlates with higher test accuracy across learning-rate, batch-size and L2 sweeps; terminal training accuracy is 1.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Embedding geometric complexity tracks held-out accuracy among these image classifiers even after training accuracy reaches 1.

fits_no_version.finding: Lower source geometric complexity accompanies lower target neural-collapse scores and higher five-shot transfer accuracy on CIFAR-FS with ResNet-18 and mini-ImageNet with VGG-16.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Lower embedding geometric complexity during pretraining predicts better few-shot transfer in the tested image-classification settings.

record.problems: The relevant test-accuracy relationship is shown in figures without numeric values in the supplied text. The authors report five random seeds for the CIFAR-10 experiment; no uncertainty estimates for the test-accuracy relationship are stated in the text.

untested.parts: Coexistence of random-label fitting and natural-label generalization, including chance-level held-out performance for random labels.
Test error as width increases beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected generalization and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under limited or broader tuning.
Large-batch held-out performance under equal epoch budgets and adaptations that remove the penalty.
Dropout's effect on held-out error across data sizes and regularization settings.
Magnitude-aware weight-perturbation sharpness versus generalization gaps and its ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
Accuracy changes after removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: The record's T2 classification mistakes a different generalization metric for a test of V7. The reported geometric-complexity association is clear qualitatively; cannot_determine refers to the listed versions and unavailable numerical values, not to an absence of that association.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and held-out accuracy on natural versus random labels.
Width sweep beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected networks and the role of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD and effects of tuning, weight decay, or optimizer switching.
Large versus small batches under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and comparisons with norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing memorized examples and measuring the resulting test-accuracy change.

rows.subject: VGG-13
rows.operation_detail: Measured training accuracy and test accuracy while sweeping learning rate; the paper reports the relationship between lower training geometric complexity and test accuracy.
rows.measure: Test accuracy; training accuracy is reported as equal to 1 at the terminal phase of training.
rows.note: The text says lower GC correlates with higher test accuracy in all settings, but the figure-only values do not give a numeric train-test gap.
rows.check: No listed version measures geometric complexity versus test accuracy. The qualitative association is explicitly reported, but exact accuracies are unavailable. Experimental details are in A.4.1; Figure 5 and its caption appear on page 18.

rows.subject: VGG-13
rows.operation_detail: Measured training accuracy and test accuracy while sweeping batch size; the paper reports the relationship between lower training geometric complexity and test accuracy.
rows.measure: Test accuracy; training accuracy is reported as equal to 1 at the terminal phase of training.
rows.note: The text says lower GC correlates with higher test accuracy in all settings, but the figure-only values do not give a numeric train-test gap.
rows.check: The batch-size sweep holds training steps at 100,000, not epochs; larger batches therefore process more training examples. It cannot establish V5's fixed-epoch penalty. Exact test accuracies are unavailable.

rows.subject: VGG-13
rows.operation_detail: Measured training accuracy and test accuracy while sweeping L2 regularization; the paper reports the relationship between lower training geometric complexity and test accuracy.
rows.measure: Test accuracy; training accuracy is reported as equal to 1 at the terminal phase of training.
rows.note: The text says lower GC correlates with higher test accuracy in all settings, but the figure-only values do not give a numeric train-test gap.
rows.check: This is an L2-regularization sweep, with no dropout comparison or magnitude-aware sharpness measurement. It tests neither V6 nor V7; exact test accuracies are unavailable.
